task.description: Predict the Form 8-K item codes a filing declares, from the text of its primary document.
task.unit: One accession. Co-filers share one filing and one label set, so n is at most 360.

acquisition.runtime: catalyst-provenance SDK Python with EdgarTools 5.58.0 (the version is checked)
acquisition.http: EdgarTools get_with_retry with the contact as its User-Agent (EDGAR_IDENTITY in the process only) and a private per-run cache (EDGAR_LOCAL_DATA_DIR)
acquisition.rate_control: EDGAR_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SEC=5 before import, plus a local pacer that starts at most five requests per second
acquisition.requests: one daily index, then per accession its .hdr.sgml header (labels) and full submission .txt (document)
acquisition.contact: Read from the file named by the SEC_CONTACT_ENV pointer (--env-file); owner-only regular file; never printed, stored or hashed into outputs
acquisition.retention: ~/.local/state/native-agent-stack/local-inference-latest-20260926/sec/<run-id>/ (0700 directories, 0600 files); manifest.json lists SHA-256, bytes and first observation per file
acquisition.complete_when: the index hash and cohort counts match, no refusal stopped the run, at most 36 acquisition failures, and at least one eligible filing
acquisition.summary_counts: summary.json adds input_chars_total, from which the expected C0 duration is computed before any window.

labels.source: FilingHeader.parse_from_sgml_text(<.hdr.sgml text before its first FILER, FILED-BY, SUBJECT-COMPANY, REPORTING-OWNER or ISSUER block>).filing_metadata['ITEMS'], split on commas, and equal to edgar.sgml.sgml_header.collect_repeated_tags(<whole header>, 'ITEMS'); a disagreement is an acquisition failure
labels.caveat: Filer-declared header metadata: not hand-checked and not frontier-model labels.
labels.cofiling_reason: EdgarTools 5.58.0 parse_from_sgml_text raises AttributeError on a header with two or more FILER blocks (reproduced offline 2026-09-26); ITEMS precede the entity blocks. The frozen cohort has 9 co-filing groups.

input.document: The first SGML <DOCUMENT> after </SEC-HEADER> whose <TYPE> equals the filing's form (8-K or 8-K/A).
input.header: The whole <SEC-HEADER> block is dropped, including its ITEM INFORMATION lines, which would reveal the labels.
input.html: Tags removed with html.parser; script, style, head, title and ix:header content dropped; block tags become line breaks; plain-text documents lose <PAGE> lines.
input.whitespace: Zero-width characters removed; each line collapsed to single spaces; empty lines dropped.
input.cap_rule: A normalized text longer than 16,000 characters keeps its first 12,000 and last 4,000 characters joined by the marker.
input.cap_justification: C0 has one 8,192-token slot. The frozen prompt is 2,470 characters without the filing (about 700 tokens with the chat template, estimated at 3.5 characters per token) and the output cap is 256 tokens, which leaves about 7,200 tokens. 16,000 characters overflow only below about 2.2 characters per token; English SEC prose runs near 4 with Qwen-family tokenizers and dense numeric tables near 3. The last 4,000 characters keep the closing items (usually 9.01) and the signature block of long documents. A request the server still rejects for length is scored as an invalid output, not excluded.

exclusions.definition: The header or submission request failed, was refused, exceeded its size cap or was not attempted after a refusal stop; or the bytes failed the native header parser, the repository's strict header identity and acceptance check, or the submission identity check; or ITEMS were malformed or repeated.
No document of the filing's form type, or its normalized text is empty.
The native header declares no ITEMS.

task.exclusion_order: The first matching reason in the listed order; every accession gets at most one.
task.n: Every eligible accession of the frozen cohort; all runnable arms score exactly the same filings.

metrics.per_filing: precision tp/(tp+fp), 0 when nothing valid is predicted; recall tp/(tp+fn); F1 2tp/(2tp+fp+fn); exact match when the predicted set equals the declared set
metrics.macro_f1: Mean per-code F1 over the codes declared by at least 5 eligible filings; the code set comes from the labels and is the same for every arm
metrics.json_valid_rate: Share of eligible filings whose whole reply is exactly one JSON object {"items": [...]} of unique code strings
metrics.fenced_json: A reply wrapped in one markdown code fence is scored for F1 but does not count as JSON-valid
metrics.invalid_output: Unparseable, wrong schema, context overflow or not attempted: the predicted set is empty
metrics.decode_tokens_per_second: timings.predicted_per_second per filing; the median over filings with an HTTP 200 reply and predicted_n >= 1
metrics.ttft_ms: timings.prompt_ms, the prompt processing time before the first generated token
metrics.cold_load_seconds: From starting the server process to its first /health 200, per segment; the first segment's is reported as the arm's
metrics.peak_device_memory: The largest whole-device memory.used in the 1 Hz nvidia-smi samples of all of the arm's segments; shared-device observation, not per-process attribution
metrics.context_overflow: HTTP 400 of type exceed_context_size_error: a per-filing invalid output, counted separately; not an arm failure
metrics.server_errors: Any other HTTP error, a malformed or oversized reply, a request deadline or an unreachable server: an event that stops the arm and fails criterion (4); the raw error body stays private

decision_rule.text: An arm replaces C0 as the production generation model only if (1) the paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 20260926) 95% lower bound of micro-F1(arm) - micro-F1(C0) is at least -0.02, (2) its median decode tokens/s exceeds C0's, (3) its JSON-valid rate is at least 0.98, and (4) it had no memory or deadline failure. Inference speed alone does not pass. C1 or C2 passing means keep the model and change only the serving profile.

bootstrap.method: Paired percentile bootstrap over filings in accession order: each resample is random.Random(20260926).choices over the filing indices, applied to both arms; micro-F1 is recomputed for each.
bootstrap.lower_bound: Nearest-rank 2.5th percentile: the 250th smallest of the 10,000 differences.

decision_rule.failure_free: Criterion (4) is scored as: the arm's segment chain is complete (every eligible filing attempted, the last segment completed) and consistent, and it has no guard event (device reserve, monitor failure, memory limit not verified, startup failure), no request or server error event, no server exit or interruption, and for every started segment valid memory evidence: memory.csv present and well formed, samples at most 30 s apart covering the server's run, none below 3,072 MiB free, and MemoryMax verified
decision_rule.control_validity: If C0 has not run, the result is inconclusive_control_not_evaluated; while C0 still has segments to run it is inconclusive_control_incomplete; if C0 failed or has any failure it is inconclusive_control_invalid. No arm replaces C0 in any of these cases.
decision_rule.selection: Among passing arms the highest median decode tokens/s is selected; ties go to the higher micro-F1, then to plan order.
decision_rule.incomplete_arms: An arm that reached a segment boundary and may still continue has outcome incomplete and cannot pass; the decision file marks final false until no arm is incomplete.

window.coordination_rule: window.sh refuses to start unless README.md contains that exact line; another session owns GPU trials until it is recorded.
window.untouched: native-stack-embeddings.service and every other unit, Windows applications and WSL distributions (never wsl --terminate or --shutdown; never the Polaris distribution)
window.guard: nvidia-smi whole-device memory.free every second, each query bounded by 10 s; a failed or timed-out query or free memory below 3,072 MiB stops only the arm's own scope.
window.isolation: systemd-run --user --scope with MemoryMax and MemorySwapMax, verified through systemctl show before the arm counts
window.retention: ~/.local/state/native-agent-stack/local-inference-latest-20260926/runs/<window>/ holds private server logs, raw replies and error bodies; window-summary.json, window.json, memory.csv, eval/metrics.json and the analysis output carry no document text.
window.production_unit_rule: window.sh accepts only nativestack-generation.service or none and refuses any other name before its preflight.
window.windows_side_prestep: Required before every window: the coordinator closes Windows-side GPU applications from the README list by exact image name and PID. window.sh never does this.
window.admission_prediction: Before stopping production, window.sh predicts free memory as the current memory.free plus production_estimated_device_mib when the unit is active, and refuses the window, touching nothing, if that is below any listed arm's admission threshold.

host_admission_arithmetic.most_free_mib_with_production_stopped: 24,143 reportable - 3,930 embeddings = 20,213 MiB, less every Windows-side allocation
host_admission_arithmetic.at_planning: About 5,766 MiB on the Windows side, so no arm would be admitted without closing applications first.

window.segments: An arm runs in segments of at most one window each. A request starts only while at least request_seconds remain before the segment's deadline, so a segment ends between requests (status segment_boundary). window.sh's next window continues that arm from its first unattempted filing, on a fresh server with the same argv, carrying earlier results verbatim and chaining each segment to the previous metrics file by SHA-256. Only a clean boundary continues; after a completed or failed segment the arm never runs again. Admission refusals and window-budget skips start nothing and may be tried in a later window.
window.request_deadline_basis: 600 s is a hang detector: the slowest legitimate C0 request, a 7,936-token prompt at 61.5 tokens/s and 256 output tokens at the p10 decode rate of 2.16 tokens/s, takes about 248 s.
window.restore_timer: Before stopping production, window.sh arms a transient user timer li26-restore-<window> that fires window_seconds later, stops this window's arm scopes and starts the production unit. The exit trap cancels it after restoring production, so it acts only if the script hung or was killed.
window.interruption: INT or TERM while a server runs records the segment as interrupted, a terminal failure; the arm is not resumed. Every exit-trap step is bounded (query 10 s, stop and start 120 s, health 330 s).

expected_duration.rates: C0 central: 100.8 prompt and 4.79 decode tokens/s; slow: 61.5 and 2.16; fast: 146.1 and 5.23 (production_timings)
expected_duration.c0_segments: Two expected (one to two for 5,000-character inputs); four only if every input were at the 16,000-character cap at the slowest rates (about 34,300 s). Each segment evaluates for at least about 8,900 s (9,600 s less cold load and the final request deadline).
expected_duration.other_arms: C1, C2 and M are expected to finish within one window together; any arm left at a boundary continues in the next.
expected_duration.check_before_windows: Compute the C0 estimate from the acquisition summary's eligible and input_chars_total before scheduling windows.
rejected_alternatives: A deterministic subsample: the task fixes n as every eligible filing.

Prompt caching of the shared instruction: for this hybrid recurrent architecture the pinned server reuses a prefix only through context checkpoints whose positions follow spacing and eviction rules driven by earlier requests (tools/server/server-context.cpp create_checkpoint at 7fe450e), so reuse and numerics would depend on filing order; every filing stays order-independent (cache_prompt false, --cache-ram 0).

window.admission_rule: Whole-device memory.free >= max(16384, estimated_device_mib + 3072) MiB immediately before load, else the arm is recorded as admission-refused: 16,384 for C0 and M, 17,151 for C1, 17,535 for C2.

failure_rule: Retain every refused, failed, stopped and interrupted attempt. No silent retry, no changed profile and no re-run to improve a result: only a clean segment boundary continues, and only from the first unattempted filing. A guard, memory-evidence, host-memory, startup, server-error, deadline or interruption failure ends that arm and fails criterion (4). Changing any frozen value needs a new plan.
claims_excluded: catalyst, incentive or trading-signal value of item codes
isolated benchmark throughput on an unshared device
any result for arms B or X
performance of the tasked C1 and C2 profiles (-ngl 99 without FFN offload; the MTP draft file)

amended_before_any_run.reason: One bounded repair round after independent review (Claude Opus and GPT-6-Astra), before any download, request or GPU window.
changes: C0 cannot cover every filing in one 3-hour window at the production profile's measured rates: every arm now runs in resumable segments of at most one window each (at most 4), continued automatically by window.sh, with the expected C0 duration predeclared.

Labels: EdgarTools 5.58.0 FilingHeader.parse_from_sgml_text raises on headers with two or more FILER blocks (the cohort has 9 co-filing groups); it now reads the header before the first entity block, cross-checked with EdgarTools collect_repeated_tags.

C1 (--gpu-layers 99) and C2 (plus the 1.3 GB MTP draft file) can essentially never be admitted beside the embeddings service and the Windows desktop; both keep every layer on the GPU but hold the dense FFN weights of blocks 0-19 on the CPU, and C2 drafts from the main file's own MTP layer. The tasked profiles are recorded in not_arms.
window.sh accepts only nativestack-generation.service or none, predicts admission before stopping production, bounds every query and wait, and arms an independent restore timer.
Any server error other than a context overflow now stops the arm and fails criterion (4); raw error bodies are kept privately.
analyze.py reads every window under the state directory and fails an arm on missing, malformed, gappy or non-covering memory samples, a sampled reserve breach or an unverified memory limit.

production_timings.scope: Production requests with server-side prompt caching and thinking enabled; only their timing lines were read. They set the expected duration; they are not results of this plan.

memory_model.source: Read-only parse of the production GGUF tensor table (2026-09-26): 65 blocks (64 layers and the blk.64 MTP layer) of 14,014.5 MiB, output.weight 994.6 MiB, token_embd.weight 682.0 MiB kept on the CPU, full attention every fourth layer.
memory_model.formula: estimate = weights on the GPU + KV cache + recurrent state + 1,024 MiB for compute buffers, the CUDA context and margin
memory_model.kv_cache: 32 MiB per full-attention layer on the GPU at context 8192 (4 KV heads x 256 x K and V x f16); the MTP layer is counted
memory_model.recurrent_state: 3.12 MiB per Gated DeltaNet layer on the GPU (48 v-heads x 128 x 128 f32 plus convolution state)
memory_model.mtp_context: 384 MiB for C2's MTP context (its KV cache and compute buffer)
memory_model.scope: Planning estimates; the guard's measured whole-device memory, not the estimate, protects other GPU users.
